title: John catena rem: signs, discourse, and the Father’s works
english: ‘[[And no one receives his testimony >> Bible:John 3:32]]’ — and yet many have received his testimony, as John himself goes on to add, saying: ‘He who has received his testimony has set his seal that God is true.’
But how can it be true, when some do receive his testimony, that ‘no one receives his testimony’? The difficulty must be resolved as follows.

Jesus, having come from above and speaking what he heard and saw, speaks a most lofty and very great testimony concerning the Father and himself; and no one receives this testimony as he himself speaks it, because the hearers, who are only beginning to receive, fall far short of the greatness of the testimony.
Yet even though no one is able to receive his testimony in this way, it is still possible to receive it as those just now coming to faith are able to receive it.

Hence ‘he who received his testimony’ is not at odds with no one’s having received it — in one sense it is not received […] — [they] who, from having received Jesus’ testimony, seal with firm assent that God is true, having learned… [the fragment breaks off]

title: John catena rem CLOSEOUT: passion and beloved disciple
english: The word ‘one’ is used in many ways — both by likeness and in many other ways: by agreement, when it says, ‘[[The multitude of those who believed were of one heart and one soul >> Bible:Acts 4:32]]’; by likeness, as when it says, ‘[[For we were all baptized in one Spirit into one body >> Bible:1 Corinthians 12:13]],’ by likeness of nature.

And as, having Adam as our beginning and head according to the nature of our birth, we are all said to have one body, so too we ascribe Christ to ourselves as head through the divine regeneration, which has become for us a type of his death and resurrection — he who rose as firstborn from the dead.
We ascribe him to ourselves as head in prefiguration of his resurrection — ‘whose members we are in part, and body, through the Spirit, being regenerated unto incorruption.’
